questions.text: Who wrote the novel The Lekki Headmaster?
questions.explanation: The Lekki Headmaster is authored by Nigerian writer Kabir Alabi Garba.

questions.text: What is the full name of the central character nicknamed 'The Lekki Headmaster'?
questions.explanation: The protagonist's name is Mr. Adewale Adebepo, usually referred to simply as Mr. Bepo.

questions.text: What school serves as the primary setting for the novel?
questions.explanation: Mr. Bepo serves as the long-standing principal at Stardom Schools, located in Lekki, Lagos.

questions.text: How many years has Mr. Bepo served at Stardom Schools?
questions.explanation: Mr. Bepo has dedicated 24 years of service to building and maintaining educational standards at Stardom Schools.

questions.text: What causes Mr. Bepo's sudden emotional breakdown on the assembly ground?
options: Threat of dismissal by the school board
Conflict over abandoning his Nigerian school legacy to relocate to the UK
News of a student's tragic accident
questions.explanation: Bepo experiences intense grief over the pressure to join his family abroad at the expense of his lifelong passion for Nigerian education.

questions.text: Who holds the position of Managing Director (MD) at Stardom Schools?
questions.explanation: Mrs. Ibidun Gloss is the business-focused Managing Director of Stardom Schools.

questions.text: Who is the Vice Principal that assists Mr. Bepo during his assembly breakdown?
questions.explanation: Mrs. Grace Apeh is the Vice Principal who steps in to support Mr. Bepo during his emotional episode.

questions.text: Where does Mr. Bepo's wife, Seri, live and work?
questions.explanation: Seri works as a healthcare professional (nurse) in the United Kingdom and urges her husband to join her.

questions.text: What major national socio-economic theme is highlighted in the book?
questions.explanation: The story centers on the widespread migration of skilled Nigerian professionals to foreign nations in search of better opportunities.

questions.text: What subject does the witty teacher, Mr. Audu, instruct?
questions.explanation: Mr. Audu is the Fine Arts teacher, noted for his satirical commentary on school management policies.

questions.text: Which student gave a captivating account of their excursion to Jos?
questions.explanation: Ikenna Egbu, an SSS 1 science student and creative poet, shared his memorable experiences from the Jos excursion.

questions.text: What attribute makes Jos a unique travel destination according to Ikenna?
options: Cool, pleasant weather and picturesque scenery
questions.explanation: Ikenna praises Jos for its temperate climate, mountainous terrain, and natural tourist sites.

questions.text: Why did Mr. Bepo repeatedly postpone renewing his passport?
options: Dread of the stressful and tedious process at the immigration office
He lost his national identification numbers
He did not know it had expired
questions.explanation: Bepo delayed his renewal because he wanted to avoid the frustrating administrative delays typical of immigration processing.

questions.text: What are the names of Mr. Bepo's two daughters living in the UK?
questions.explanation: His two daughters residing in the UK alongside his wife are Nike and Kike.

questions.text: What is the main purpose of 'Pen Day' at Stardom Schools?
options: Open Day where parents review student progress with teachers
questions.explanation: Pen Day functions as the school's Open Day, allowing parents to inspect student workbooks and discuss academic growth.

questions.text: Which two students share a prolonged, intense rivalry throughout the story?
questions.explanation: Banky and Tosh are long-standing academic and personal rivals dating back to their junior school days.

questions.text: What landmark was visited during the school excursion to Badagry?
questions.explanation: The Badagry educational tour covered key historical sites, including the First Storey Building, the slave trade route, and the Point of No Return.

questions.text: What does the 'Point of No Return' symbolize in the narrative?
options: The tragic history of the transatlantic slave trade and historical dislocation
questions.explanation: It symbolizes the painful history of forced human displacement, mirroring modern economic displacement and migration.

questions.text: What project was the school's Invention Club working to complete?
questions.explanation: The student Invention Club demonstrated tech innovation by fabricating a working local telephone system prototype.

questions.text: What is the ultimate resolution of Mr. Bepo's travel journey?
options: He gets turned back at immigration in Heathrow
He heads to the airport but decides to turn back and remain dedicated to Stardom Schools
He retires to live in Jos
questions.explanation: At the climax, Bepo chooses his sense of duty and passion for Nigerian education over relocation, making a dramatic return to his school.

questions.text: What figure of speech is 'The morning assembly was under a world of tears'?
questions.explanation: Directly equating the atmosphere to a 'world of tears' without 'like' or 'as' forms a metaphor.

questions.text: How would you describe Mrs. Ibidun Gloss's administrative style?
questions.explanation: Mrs. Gloss runs the school like a corporate business, prioritizing financial returns, prestige, and strict standards.

questions.text: What monthly salary was Mr. Bepo earning as principal?
questions.explanation: The novel states his earnings were ₦400,000, illustrating the economic disparity driving skilled workers to earn foreign currencies.

questions.text: What primary conflict drives the narrative of The Lekki Headmaster?
options: Personal Duty/Patriotism vs. Family Migration Demands
questions.explanation: The core dilemma centers on Bepo's internal battle between his duty to educate local youth and family pressure to emigrate.

questions.text: Which character provides frequent comic relief regarding staff welfare?
questions.explanation: Mr. Audu uses humor and sharp commentary to critique administration policies and ease staff tension.

questions.text: Why did parents often dread 'Pen Days' at Stardom Schools?
options: High admission fees were collected that day
Teachers openly presented detailed academic and behavioral complaints about students
Students were subjected to physical labor
questions.explanation: Pen Days exposed student shortcomings, leading to awkward or difficult discussions between parents, teachers, and students.

questions.text: What core motivation drives Mr. Bepo's deep passion for teaching?
options: Shaping young minds and leaving a lasting legacy in his country
Securing an easy route for foreign travel
questions.explanation: Bepo views teaching as a sacred calling to build future generations rather than a mere income source.

questions.text: How does Seri attempt to convince Bepo to move to the UK?
options: By offering to buy him a luxury car
Emphasizing economic stability, security, and family togetherness
questions.explanation: Seri points out the foreign exchange advantage, security, and the necessity of raising their family together abroad.

questions.text: What attitude do the elite parents in Lekki generally display toward teachers?
options: Entitlement, high expectations, and demanding behavior
questions.explanation: Elite parents expect premium results for their high fees and often treat school staff with high demands and entitlement.

questions.text: What literary tone dominates the descriptions of the Badagry slave trade sites?
questions.explanation: The Badagry excursion chapters evoke solemn reflection on human suffering and historical injustice.

questions.text: What role does Mrs. Grace Apeh play in maintaining school balance?
options: She acts as a mediator between strict management and the teaching staff
She manages the school's social media accounts
questions.explanation: As Vice Principal, Mrs. Apeh buffers management pressure while supporting staff and students emotionally.

questions.text: What social status is associated with the students attending Stardom Schools?
questions.explanation: Stardom Schools caters to wealthy Lekki residents, reflecting high tuition fees and privileged backgrounds.

questions.text: What theme is illustrated by the Invention Club's phone prototype project?
options: Youth potential, ingenuity, and the importance of STEM education
questions.explanation: The project showcases student talent and resourcefulness when given opportunities in science and technology.

questions.text: Why is Mr. Bepo referred to as a 'headmaster' despite heading a secondary school?
options: It is his official legal title
An affectionate, humorous nod to his classic leadership style and love for old TV drama
A translation error by school owners
A title awarded by the Ministry of Education
questions.explanation: The title stems from his traditional approach and fond references to the iconic television show The Village Headmaster.

questions.text: What is the effect of the 'Japa' trend on the teaching staff at Stardom Schools?
options: Frequent teacher turnover and understaffing as educators leave the country
questions.explanation: The continuous emigration of qualified teachers creates staffing shortages and destabilizes school planning.

questions.text: How does Ikenna Egbu present his essay on Jos?
options: Through a bland reading of notes
Through poetic language and vivid descriptive imagery
questions.explanation: Ikenna uses creative flair, poetry, and rich descriptions to engage the assembly.

questions.text: What obstacle does Mr. Bepo face when attempting his passport renewal?
options: System outages, long queues, and bureaucratic delays
Complete closure of all passport offices
questions.explanation: The novel depicts administrative bottlenecks, overcrowded centers, and delays in government processing.

questions.text: What reaction do the students have to news of Mr. Bepo's potential departure?
options: Deep sorrow, anxiety, and widespread emotional outpourings
questions.explanation: Students view Bepo as a father figure, making his potential departure a source of distress across the school.

questions.text: What literary device is used in describing the school as 'a factory of future leaders'?
questions.explanation: Describing the school directly as a 'factory' without using comparison words like 'as' or 'like' forms a metaphor.

questions.text: What lesson does the Badagry excursion teach the students?
options: The historical cost of human oppression and the value of freedom
questions.explanation: Visiting historical slave sites confronts students with the tragic realities of past human exploitation.

questions.text: How does Mrs. Ibidun Gloss view teacher resignations?
options: As routine operational costs to be managed by hiring replacements
As reasons to shut down the school
questions.explanation: She maintains a strictly business-oriented mindset, viewing turnover as an operational issue rather than an emotional crisis.

questions.text: What setting contrast is highlighted between Lekki and other Lagos neighborhoods?
options: Wealth and modern infrastructure versus crowded, struggling urban centers
Complete agricultural land versus forest reserves
Historical monuments versus new industrial zones
questions.explanation: The book contrasts the affluent, private enclave of Lekki with the economic struggles of broader Lagos.

questions.text: What quality makes Banky stand out as a student?
options: Exceptional academic performance coupled with a competitive edge
Lack of interest in school competitions
questions.explanation: Banky is highly driven, intelligent, and determined to top his class, fueling his rivalry with Tosh.

questions.text: What factor creates tension between Mr. Bepo and his wife, Seri?
options: Divergent views on living in Nigeria versus settling permanently in the UK
Choices regarding their children's career paths
questions.explanation: Seri wants the family united in the UK for economic security, while Bepo remains emotionally tied to his educational work in Nigeria.

questions.text: What figure of speech is present in 'The news hit him like a lightning bolt'?
questions.explanation: Comparing the impact of the news to a lightning bolt using the word 'like' constitutes a simile.

questions.text: What subject does the school's Invention Club fall under structurally?
questions.explanation: The club operates within practical science and technology education, fostering practical invention.

questions.text: How does the narrative view the decision to 'Japa'?
options: As a complex choice driven by survival, search for stability, and systemic challenges
As an easy shortcut to overnight riches
As a trend forced by government mandates
questions.explanation: The author presents migration empathetically, showing the difficult trade-offs individuals make when fleeing socio-economic hardship.

questions.text: What is the significance of the title The Lekki Headmaster?
options: It highlights a government political office
It blends traditional educational dedication with a modern, affluent Lagos setting
It refers to a historical colonial ruler
It denotes a character in a legendary folk tale
questions.explanation: The title captures Bepo's classic, committed educator persona within the modern private education hub of Lekki.

questions.text: What key message does Mr. Bepo deliver to students during assembly addresses?
options: Integrity, national commitment, hard work, and moral character
questions.explanation: Bepo consistently emphasizes character development, self-reliance, and devotion to personal and national growth.

questions.text: What final choice defines Mr. Bepo's character development at the end of the book?
options: He resigns to start a private business abroad
He reaffirms his commitment to Nigerian education and stays at Stardom Schools
He leaves teaching to enter local politics
He moves to Jos to retire comfortably
questions.explanation: Bepo turns back from his trip abroad, prioritizing his educational calling and commitment to building young lives in Nigeria.

questions.text: What ritual occurred at the morning assembly at Stardom Schools on Tuesdays and Thursdays?
options: Recitation of the second stanza of the National Anthem
A short drama by the drama club
questions.explanation: On Tuesdays and Thursdays, the assembly routine specifically featured student recitations of the second stanza of Nigeria's National Anthem.

questions.text: What was the boarding house fee per session at Stardom Schools before management reduced it?
questions.explanation: The text notes that before adjustments were made, the boarding fees stood at ₦163,000 per session.

questions.text: Who instructed the staff to conclude the assembly when Mr. Bepo burst into tears?
questions.explanation: Vice Principal Mrs. Grace Apeh stepped in immediately to take control and instruct that the assembly be brought to an order.

questions.text: Why did the Vice Principal contact the MD after Mr. Bepo's emotional episode?
options: To arrange an emergency staff meeting
Because parents were calling the school with concerns after students reported the incident
To announce the principal's immediate retirement
questions.explanation: Word spread fast through students, leading worried parents to make inquiry calls to the administrative office.

questions.text: How did the students come to nickname Mr. Bepo 'Principoo'?
options: It was a term of endearment blending 'Principal' and his affectionate demeanor
A mocking phrase invented by junior students
A title given to him by the PTA board
A nickname derived from his former school in Beesway
questions.explanation: Students affectionately called him 'Principoo' as an informal, friendly variation of 'Principal'.

questions.text: What parent offered to assist Mr. Bepo with his visa application process?
questions.explanation: Mrs. Ignatius, a parent with international ties, encouraged Bepo to relocate and assisted him with visa arrangements.

questions.text: What former teaching institution did Mr. Bepo work at before joining Stardom Schools?
questions.explanation: Bepo previously worked at Beesway Group of Schools, where he encountered unethical practices by the school management.

questions.text: Why did Mr. Bepo leave his former position at Beesway Group of Schools?
options: Moral disagreement with the proprietor over unethical and ritualistic practices
He was fired for poor performance
questions.explanation: Bepo resigned after witnessing disturbing, unethical practices involving ritualism by the school's director.

questions.text: What physical habit was Mr. Bepo known for while addressing students at assembly?
options: Placing his left hand in his pocket while speaking
Walking back and forth across the stage
questions.explanation: Bepo had a signature posture of keeping his left hand in his pocket during speeches.

questions.text: What favorite signature phrase did Mr. Bepo frequently use when explaining concepts?
questions.explanation: Bepo frequently introduced conditions in his talks using the economic phrase 'other things being equal...'.

questions.text: What proverb did Mr. Bepo repeat to remind students of the worth of learning?
options: 'If you say education is too expensive, try ignorance!'
'Failure to plan is planning to fail'
'The pen is mightier than the sword'
questions.explanation: Bepo often used this famous quote to urge students to appreciate the value of schooling.

questions.text: Why was Mr. Bepo's initial British visa application rejected?
options: The entry clearance officer doubted why someone with a stable, successful career would abandon it
questions.explanation: The immigration official found it suspicious that an established school principal would abandon a 24-year career.

questions.text: What caused student Bibi Ladele to have nightmares in Chapter 4?
options: Fear of Mr. Ayesoro, the Government teacher with prominent facial marks
A horror movie she watched at home
questions.explanation: Bibi had severe frights after encountering Mr. Ayesoro (nicknamed 'Mr. Owala'), leading to nightmares.

questions.text: How did management resolve the issue surrounding student Bibi's fear of Mr. Ayesoro?
options: They transferred Mr. Ayesoro to Stardom Hub, the real estate branch
They expelled Bibi from the school
They forced Bibi to attend counseling sessions
questions.explanation: To protect enrollment and appease the parent, management reassigned Mr. Ayesoro to Stardom Hub.

questions.text: What company division exists alongside Stardom Schools under the Stardom Group?
options: Stardom Hub (Property and Real Estate wing)
questions.explanation: Stardom Group consists of the educational institutions and Stardom Hub, its real estate wing.

questions.text: What secret habit did Managing Director Mrs. Ibidun Gloss keep during school breaks?
options: Eating special snacks in her car
Taking a short nap in a hidden room inside her office
questions.explanation: Mrs. Gloss secretly took short power naps in a hidden adjoining room in her office to recharge.

questions.text: Why was English teacher Mr. Fafore summoned to the MD's office on Pen Day?
options: A parent accused him of incompetence regarding English instruction
He accepted cash gifts directly from students
questions.explanation: A parent complained to the MD about Mr. Fafore's teaching method, prompting an immediate summons.

questions.text: Who was Chief David Aje in the context of Stardom Schools?
options: The late founder of Stardom Schools and father to Mrs. Ibidun Gloss
The former principal before Mr. Bepo
questions.explanation: Chief David Aje founded Stardom Schools, which was later managed by his daughter, Mrs. Gloss.

questions.text: How did many teachers privately view 'Pen Days'?
options: With enthusiasm because of monetary bonuses
With dread, due to lengthy parent complaints and scrutiny
As a waste of academic hours
questions.explanation: Teachers often found Pen Days exhausting because parents used the time to vent criticisms.

questions.text: What monetary gift did the school management present to Mr. Bepo during his send-off?
questions.explanation: Mrs. Gloss presented Mr. Bepo with a farewell cheque gift of $10,000 in recognition of his service.

questions.text: Who is Jide in the context of Mr. Bepo's personal life?
options: The grandson of Mr. Bepo's landlord, whom Bepo mentored
A junior clerk at Stardom Hub
questions.explanation: Jide is the landlord's grandson, serving as an example of Bepo's community mentorship.

questions.text: What recurrence in Mr. Bepo's dreams symbolized his mental conflict about migrating?
options: Recurring nightmares relating to historical slave trade routes and loss of home
Dreams of losing his property in Nigeria
questions.explanation: Bepo experienced symbolic nightmares linking modern forced migration with historical slave trade memories.

questions.text: What field of study does Mr. Oyelana teach at Stardom Schools?
questions.explanation: Mr. Oyelana is one of the trusted colleagues Bepo confided in, serving as the CRK teacher.

questions.text: What factor created a rift during the prefect elections at Stardom Schools?
options: Student rivalry between Banky and Tosh
questions.explanation: The competition between Banky and Tosh spilled over into the prefect elections, creating factional rivalry.

questions.text: What is the central tone of Kabir Alabi Garba's narrative?
questions.explanation: The novel adopts a reflective tone that encourages moral lessons on integrity, purpose, and education.

questions.text: What does the 'Japa' phenomenon literally translate to in Yoruba slang?
options: To run, flee, or escape quickly
questions.explanation: 'Japa' is a Yoruba slang word meaning to flee or run away, commonly used for foreign migration.

questions.text: How did stories of Nigerian migrants in the UK affect Mr. Bepo's perspective?
options: They made him expect effortless wealth
They exposed the reality that professional qualifications often get downgraded abroad
They convinced him to abandon education completely
They made him fear air travel
questions.explanation: Migration tales revealed that qualified professionals (e.g., principals, lecturers) often took low-skilled jobs abroad.

questions.text: Which character represents the drive to balance profit with academic reputation?
questions.explanation: As Managing Director, Mrs. Gloss maintains high operational standards to safeguard profit and reputation.

questions.text: What literary device is exemplified in 'The news hit the school like a thunderclap'?
questions.explanation: The explicit comparison using 'like' makes this a simile.

questions.text: What lesson does Mr. Bepo's final return to Stardom Schools convey?
options: Moving abroad is always a failure
True fulfillment lies in staying true to one's calling and sense of impact
Schools should not pay high salaries
Real estate is more lucrative than teaching
questions.explanation: Bepo's return highlights that purpose, mentorship, and legacy can outweigh material allure abroad.

questions.text: How are parents' expectations characterized at Stardom Schools?
questions.explanation: Paying premium fees in Lekki, parents held demanding expectations regarding their children's care and grades.

questions.text: What was Mr. Bepo's primary reason for founding the Invention Club?
options: To nurture practical skills, creativity, and scientific innovation in students
To generate income by selling student projects
questions.explanation: Bepo created the club to bridge theory and practical innovation, encouraging hands-on technology skills.

questions.text: How did the teaching staff react to Mr. Bepo's resignation?
options: With sadness, feeling they were losing a supportive leader and shield
questions.explanation: Teachers respected Bepo's leadership, knowing he protected staff interests against unfair administrative pressures.

questions.text: What theme does the relocation of Seri and her daughters represent early in the novel?
options: Family separation due to socio-economic push factors
questions.explanation: Seri's initial departure illustrates how economic pressures pull family members abroad separately.

questions.text: What literary device is present in 'The silence in the hall was deafening'?
questions.explanation: Combining two contradictory terms ('silence' and 'deafening') forms an oxymoron.

questions.text: What is the location of the Black Heritage Museum visited during the school trip?
questions.explanation: The Black Heritage Museum is located in Badagry, Lagos State.

questions.text: What value does Mr. Bepo prioritize over personal wealth throughout his career?
options: Moral integrity and service to youth development
questions.explanation: Bepo's choices continuously show that moral duty and student welfare rank above financial gain.

questions.text: Who took over the immediate running of assembly duties during Mr. Bepo's absence?
questions.explanation: As Vice Principal, Mrs. Apeh managed administrative duties and assembly routines.

questions.text: What atmosphere characterized the send-off ceremony for Mr. Bepo?
questions.explanation: The send-off combined deep gratitude and sorrow over his departure alongside cultural performances.

questions.text: How does the novel depict the administrative process at the Nigerian passport office?
questions.explanation: The passport acquisition scenes illustrate delays and crowds typical of public administrative systems.

questions.text: What primary message does the novel send regarding Nigerian education?
options: Dedicated educators are essential for national development despite systemic hurdles
Western education is superior in every way
Vocational skills should completely replace academics
questions.explanation: The story underscores that committed teachers remain the backbone of societal growth.

questions.text: What was the main cause of the dispute between Banky and Tosh?
questions.explanation: Their ongoing rivalry stemmed from competing to be top academic performers and class leaders.

questions.text: What term best describes Mr. Audu's role among the teachers?
options: Comic relief and candid social critic
questions.explanation: Mr. Audu eases tension with humor while offering insightful observations on school management.

questions.text: What is the narrative point of view used in The Lekki Headmaster?
questions.explanation: The story is told by an all-knowing third-person narrator who reveals the thoughts and feelings of multiple characters.

questions.text: Why did Mr. Bepo feel an 'emotional void' when heading to the airport?
options: He felt he was abandoning his true life purpose and students in Nigeria
questions.explanation: Leaving his life's work at Stardom created an inner conflict that foreign travel could not fulfill.

questions.text: What figure of speech is present in 'The wind whispered through the empty corridors'?
questions.explanation: Giving the inanimate human attribute of 'whispering' to the wind is personification.

questions.text: What impact did the 'Point of No Return' visit have on the students?
options: It gave them a deeper understanding of historical sacrifice and resilience
It made them want to travel abroad immediately
It inspired them to study geography exclusively
questions.explanation: The visit provided an emotional history lesson on the cost of human exploitation.

questions.text: What role did Mrs. Ignatius play in the story's progression?
options: She acted as a catalyst pushing Bepo toward the visa application process
She replaced Mrs. Gloss as MD
questions.explanation: Mrs. Ignatius encouraged Bepo to pursue relocation and guided his visa effort.

questions.text: How does the novel depict the contrast between public and private education in Nigeria?
options: Private schools are depicted as well-resourced but commercialized, while public systems suffer from neglect
Public schools are shown to be superior in every metric
There is no difference depicted between them
Private schools are shown as entirely affordable to all classes
questions.explanation: The narrative highlights how private institutions offer better facilities but face high tuition and profit pressures.

questions.text: What is the ultimate message of The Lekki Headmaster regarding national development?
options: Development is impossible in developing nations
Building a nation requires dedicated individuals willing to invest in human capital at home
Technology will solve all problems without human effort
questions.explanation: Bepo's final choice underscores that true nation-building depends on selfless individuals nurturing the next generation.

questions.text: What grammatical controversy arose between the Managing Director and the English teacher, Mr. Fafore?
options: The expression 'Ade as well as Jide comes'
The use of active versus passive voice
questions.explanation: Mrs. Ibidun Gloss accused Mr. Fafore of incompetence over the sentence 'Ade as well as Jide comes,' mistakenly believing the verb should be plural ('come'), until Mr. Bepo defended the rule of proximity and singular agreement with 'as well as'.

questions.text: Where does English teacher Mr. Fafore reside, illustrating his grueling daily commute?
questions.explanation: Mr. Fafore lives in Ifo, Ogun State, waking up at 4:00 am daily to travel to Stardom Schools in Lekki, highlighting the sacrifices made by Nigerian educators.

questions.text: What monthly salary was Mr. Fafore earning at Stardom Schools as an English teacher?
questions.explanation: Despite his dedication and long commute, Mr. Fafore earned a monthly salary of ₦175,000.

questions.text: What award did Mr. Fafore win twice at Stardom Schools?
questions.explanation: Mr. Fafore was recognized twice with the Most Punctual Teacher Award despite traveling all the way from Ogun State.

questions.text: What scandal ruined Mrs. Ignatius's plans to relocate her family to the UK?
options: A DNA test revealing her husband was not the biological father of her child
questions.explanation: The visa process required a DNA test, which exposed that her husband was not the biological father of their child (Favour), leading to the rejection of their visa application and a marital crisis.

questions.text: What skills had Mrs. Ignatius acquired in preparation for her expected life in the UK?
questions.explanation: Anticipating her move abroad, Mrs. Ignatius trained in tailoring and hairdressing to secure side incomes in the UK.

questions.text: What company does Mr. Ibe Ignatius work for as a manager?
questions.explanation: Mr. Ibe Ignatius is an oil company manager who strongly advocated for the 'Japa' philosophy until his family visa was stalled.

questions.text: Who is Tosh's father in The Lekki Headmaster?
questions.explanation: Tosh (Ogba Junior) is the son of Chief Didi Ogba.

questions.text: What past controversy surrounding Chief Didi Ogba was brought up during the school prefect election speeches?
options: His trial and acquittal in a financial embezzlement case
questions.explanation: Banky publicly insulted Tosh by referencing Chief Didi Ogba's past detention and trial over embezzlement allegations, causing chaos during the speeches.

questions.text: Who is the Physics teacher who doubles as a pastor and offered prayers for Mr. Bepo?
questions.explanation: Pastor Ope Wande is the Physics teacher at Stardom Schools who offered spiritual support to Mr. Bepo during his emotional moments.

questions.text: What action did Nurse Titi take when Mr. Bepo broke down on the assembly ground?
options: She gave him water and offered him a handkerchief
She asked the students to sing a hymn
questions.explanation: Nurse Titi rushed to Mr. Bepo's side, handing him a handkerchief to wipe his tears and attending to his comfort.

questions.text: What was the name of the innovative project launched by the school's Invention Club?
questions.explanation: The Invention Club named their local telephone manufacturing experiment 'The Breath Project'.

questions.text: What materials did the Invention Club use for 'The Breath Project'?
options: Recycled materials and salvaged electronic components
questions.explanation: 'The Breath Project' focused on sustainability and local ingenuity by utilizing recycled and salvaged components.

questions.text: Who was the agent that assisted Mr. Bepo with navigating the immigration office during his passport renewal?
questions.explanation: Tai acted as a passport processing agent who helped Bepo bypass long queues and bureaucratic delays.

questions.text: What nickname was given to Mr. Ayesoro, the Government teacher, by students?
questions.explanation: Students nicknamed Mr. Ayesoro 'Mr. Owala' due to his prominent facial (tribal) marks.

questions.text: Why did Mrs. Ladele come to Stardom Schools to complain about Mr. Ayesoro?
options: He gave her daughter failing marks in Government
Her daughter, Bibi, was having nightmares caused by fear of his facial marks
He flogged her daughter during class
He demanded money for extra lessons
questions.explanation: Mrs. Ladele complained that Mr. Ayesoro's facial marks terrified her young daughter, causing recurring nightmares.

questions.text: What financial restriction did Mrs. Ibidun Gloss enforce on the staff cooperative society?
options: Banning staff members from saving monthly
Restricting maximum borrowing limits after noticing teachers accumulating substantial funds
Forcing all staff to bank with the school's preferred bank
questions.explanation: Mrs. Gloss restricted cooperative borrowing to maintain management control when she realized staff were gaining financial independence.

questions.text: Who is Mr. Amos in the administrative structure of Stardom Schools?
questions.explanation: Mr. Amos serves as the efficient accountant at Stardom Schools.

questions.text: What figure of speech is present in 'The heat at the passport office was a furnace'?
questions.explanation: Directly equating the heat to a 'furnace' without 'like' or 'as' constitutes a metaphor.

questions.text: What was Mr. Bepo's reaction when Mrs. Gloss nearly dismissed Mr. Fafore over grammar?
options: He supported the MD's decision to dismiss him
He firmly defended Mr. Fafore's grammatical correctness and saved his job
He remained silent to protect his own position
He asked Mr. Fafore to apologize publicly
questions.explanation: Bepo stood up for the English teacher, explaining the correct rules of concord to Mrs. Gloss and preventing Fafore's wrongful termination.

questions.text: What cultural performance was rendered during the climax of Mr. Bepo's farewell party?
questions.explanation: The event culminated in a symbolic Canoe Dance, symbolizing journey, movement, and survival across waters.

questions.text: How much was Mr. Bepo offered as a starting salary for his prospective teaching job in the UK?
questions.explanation: The UK offer promised roughly £3,000 monthly, drastically higher in naira terms than his ₦400,000 principal salary in Nigeria.

questions.text: Who was Mr. Ogunwale in relation to Mr. Bepo's departure journey?
options: The driver who drove Mr. Bepo toward the airport
The immigration officer who stamped his passport
questions.explanation: Mr. Ogunwale was the trusted driver who conveyed Mr. Bepo on his emotional trip toward Murtala Muhammed International Airport.

questions.text: What mistake did Mr. Bepo make regarding his flight details on his initial planned departure date?
options: He went to the wrong airport terminal
He misread the flight departure time on his ticket
He forgot his international passport at home
He showed up a day after the flight had departed
questions.explanation: Bepo misread the departure time on his flight itinerary, delaying his departure schedule.

questions.text: What irony is embedded in Mr. Bepo's decision to return to Stardom Schools at the end of the novel?
options: He returned only to find out he had been replaced and demoted
After months of pressure, visa hassles, and a grand send-off, he voluntarily abandoned the journey at the final moment to return to his true calling
He returned because his plane was forced to land due to bad weather
His wife returned to Nigeria on the same day he left
questions.explanation: Situational irony occurs because despite elaborate farewells and a $10,000 cheque, his deep commitment to Nigerian education led him back home.

questions.text: What was the name of the proprietor who ran the occultic Beesway Group of Schools?
questions.explanation: Egi Meko was the unethical proprietor of Beesway Group of Schools whose ritualistic practices forced Bepo to resign years earlier.

questions.text: Why did Mr. Bepo refuse to participate in the practices at Beesway Group of Schools?
options: He was not paid enough salary
His high moral standards and religious values forbade compromising integrity for success
He wanted to buy the school from the owner
The school was located too far from his house
questions.explanation: Bepo's core character trait is uncompromising moral integrity, leading him to reject unethical practices regardless of financial benefits.

questions.text: What character type does Mrs. Ibidun Gloss represent in the narrative?
options: A pragmatic, corporate-style administrator balancing profit and prestige
questions.explanation: Mrs. Gloss represents private sector educational management focused on profitability, reputation, and strict standards.

questions.text: How did student Ikenna Egbu describe the Jos wildlife park during his presentation?
options: As a neglected and dangerous wasteland
As a serene, rich sanctuary showcasing nature's beauty
questions.explanation: Ikenna vividly described the Jos wildlife park with poetic admiration, emphasizing its calm environment and scenic value.

questions.text: What figure of speech is 'The classroom was a hive of bees before the teacher walked in'?
questions.explanation: Comparing the noisy classroom directly to a 'hive of bees' is a metaphor.

questions.text: What did the school present to top-performing students on Pen Days?
options: Certificates of excellence, books, and commendation letters
questions.explanation: Academic achievements were celebrated through commendations, books, and recognition certificates during Open Days.

questions.text: What social issue is reflected through Mr. Fafore's early morning commute from Ogun State?
options: The high cost of housing in elite Lagos zones forcing middle-class workers to live in distant suburbs
The failure of private car manufacturing
questions.explanation: Fafore's long commute from Ifo to Lekki mirrors real-world housing unaffordability in commercial hubs for working-class professionals.

questions.text: What reason did Mrs. Gloss give for transferring Mr. Ayesoro to Stardom Hub?
options: He was unqualified to teach Government
To prevent losing wealthy parents who threatened to withdraw students due to his appearance
To give him a salary promotion
Because he requested a career change to real estate
questions.explanation: Management prioritized customer (parental) satisfaction and retention over staff fairness by moving him away from classroom teaching.

questions.text: What lesson did Mr. Bepo teach Jide during their private mentoring sessions?
options: How to make quick profits in business
The value of honesty, diligence, discipline, and devotion to personal growth
Techniques for passing exams without studying
Strategies for migrating to Europe quickly
questions.explanation: Bepo mentored Jide in character, academic excellence, and personal discipline.

questions.text: What is the symbolic meaning of the 'banner' displayed during Mr. Bepo's send-off?
options: Recognition of his 24 years of transformative leadership and service
An advertisement for Stardom Group real estate
A warning notice to new staff members
A political protest banner against migration laws
questions.explanation: The farewell banner honored his extensive, dedicated service to the school community.

questions.text: What literary device is used in the phrase 'Japa has swallowed our best brains'?
questions.explanation: Giving the abstract concept of 'Japa' the human action of 'swallowing' is personification.

questions.text: How did the teachers react when they heard Mr. Bepo was offered $10,000 as a farewell gift?
options: They were happy for him, acknowledging he earned every bit of it through 24 years of devotion
They demanded that the money be shared among all staff
They suspected the money was counterfeit
questions.explanation: Staff members admired Bepo and felt the cash award was a well-deserved honor for his decades of service.

questions.text: Why did Mr. Bepo feel uncomfortable with the grand farewell party thrown for him?
options: His heart was still torn about leaving his true calling and students
He thought the event cost too much money
He wanted a private dinner instead
questions.explanation: The celebration heightened his internal conflict because he was emotionally attached to his work and country.

questions.text: Which student represented artistic and poetic expression in the novel?
questions.explanation: Ikenna Egbu demonstrated talent in creative writing, poetry, and expressive public speaking.

questions.text: What attitude did Mr. Bepo display toward material wealth throughout his tenure?
options: Contentment, prioritizing impact and legacy over luxury
Willingness to compromise rules for bribes
questions.explanation: Bepo lived modestly and focused on moral integrity and educational legacy rather than chasing wealth.

questions.text: What major administrative flaw of Mrs. Ibidun Gloss is exposed in the novel?
options: Impulsive decision-making based on parental pressure without full investigations
Inability to pay staff salaries on time
questions.explanation: Mrs. Gloss often made hasty decisions—such as almost firing Fafore or reassigning Ayesoro—to appease rich parents.

questions.text: How did Mr. Bepo view his role as a principal?
options: As a routine administrative desk job
As a mentorship calling to build future leaders and transform lives
As a temporary stepping stone to a political career
As a way to gain social status in Lekki
questions.explanation: Bepo viewed school leadership as a sacred duty to shape young minds for national progress.

questions.text: What figure of speech is present in 'The assignment was a piece of cake for Ikenna'?
questions.explanation: Comparing an easy task to a 'piece of cake' is an idiomatic metaphor.

questions.text: What theme is illustrated by the conflict between Banky and Tosh during elections?
options: Youthful ambition, rivalry, and the influence of adult baggage on children
questions.explanation: Their contest showed how personal competition and parental history influence student behavior.

questions.text: What does the name 'Stardom Schools' symbolize?
options: The aspiration to groom brilliant, elite, and successful future leaders
questions.explanation: The name highlights the institution's mission to produce high-achieving 'star' students.

questions.text: How did the visa immigration officer react during Mr. Bepo's second visa interview?
options: He approved it after Bepo clearly established his family reunion purpose and documentation
questions.explanation: After satisfying immigration requirements regarding documentation and family reunification, his visa was granted.

questions.text: What reason made Seri persistent about Bepo joining her in the UK?
options: She wanted him to buy a house in London
She believed living together as a family was essential for raising their children properly
She wanted him to study for a PhD
She needed him to run a business with her
questions.explanation: Seri emphasized family unity, moral support, and raising their children together in a stable environment.

questions.text: What was the reaction of the airport driver, Mr. Ogunwale, when Mr. Bepo ordered him to turn back to Lekki?
options: He was shocked and tried to persuade him, but ultimately respected his decision
He refused and dropped him on the highway
He reported him to his wife
He demanded double the transport fee
questions.explanation: Ogunwale was surprised by the sudden change of heart but understood Bepo's deep attachment to his life work.

questions.text: What key transformation occurs in Mr. Bepo's character arc by the end of the book?
options: He moves from self-doubt and external compliance back to firm conviction and purpose
He becomes bitter toward his family
He decides to retire from working completely
He adopts Mrs. Gloss's profit-first mindset
questions.explanation: Bepo resolves his internal struggle by choosing his genuine calling over external societal expectations.

questions.text: What core message does Kabir Alabi Garba convey to young readers through The Lekki Headmaster?
options: Wealth is the only measure of career success
Every individual must seek ways to travel abroad at all costs
Passion, integrity, and patriotism in one's vocation build lasting legacy and societal progress
Administrative power should never be questioned
questions.explanation: The novel asserts that true fulfillment and national renewal stem from integrity, dedication, and service to one's community.
